assignment:
Your principal is considering changing school policy so that students may not participate in sports or other activities unless they have at least a grade B average. Many students have a grade C average. 
She would like to hear the students' views on this possible policy change. Write a letter to your principal arguing for or against requiring at least a grade B average to participate in sports or other activities. Be sure to support your arguments with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the new policy that says students have to have a B average to play sports or be in clubs. I understand that you want kids to get better grades, but I think this rule will hurt more students than it helps.

First of all, a lot of students have a C average, and a C is still a passing grade. These kids are doing ok in their classes, but they would get kicked off the teams and clubs that they love. For some students sports is the only reason they even want to come to school. If we take that away from them they might stop trying and their grades might get even worse.

Second, activities teach you stuff that you cant learn in a classroom. Being on a team teaches you how to work with other people and be disciplined. Yearbook and drama club teach you responsibility and how to manage your time. Someone might be bad at math but really good at music or being a leader. This policy ignores what those students are good at.

Third, activities can actually help students get better grades. A lot of athletes keep their schedules organized because practice is right after school. Coaches and advisors also check on their students and tell them to study. If they dont have that, kids who are struggling might not have anybody pushing them to do better.

Instead of a B average, I think a C average would be more fair, and the school could give free tutoring to students who fall behind. That still shows that grades matter, but it helps students instead of punishing them.

I hope you think about this before you decide. I really think it would be a better choice for our school. Thank you for listening to the students.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the new rule that says students need a B average to play sports or join clubs. I know you want kids to get good grades, but I think this rule is unfair and hurts a lot of students.

First, many students have a C average. A C is a passing grade. Those students are doing okay in their classes. They would still be removed from the teams and clubs they love. For some kids, sports are the only reason they come to school. If we take that away, they might stop trying in class, and then their grades could get worse.

Second, activities teach things you can't learn in a classroom. A team teaches you to work together and show up on time. The yearbook staff and the drama club teach responsibility. A student might struggle in math, but that same student can be a great musician or a strong leader on the field. Those students have talents too.

Third, activities help kids with their grades. Many athletes keep a schedule because practice is right after school. Coaches and advisors check in on their students and tell them to study. Without that, some students would have nobody pushing them.

Instead of a B average, I think a C average is a fair rule. The school could also offer free tutoring for students who need it. That way grades still count, and students get help from the school instead of getting shut out.

Please think about all of the students before you decide. Thank you for reading my letter.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
